etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English accompanien, from Old French acompagner (“to associate with”), from compaing (“companion”), nominative singular of compaignon (“companion”). See company.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To go with or attend as a companion or associate; to keep company with; to go along with.

quote.citation: 1804, Richard Glover, (Please provide the book title or journal name):
quote.text: The Persian dames, […] / In sumptuous cars, accompanied his march.

quote.citation: 1581, Philip Sidney, An Apology of Poetry, or a Defense of Poesy, Book I:
quote.text: They are never alone that are accompanied with noble thoughts.

quote.citation: 1979, Thomas Babington Macaulay, The History of England:
quote.text: He was accompanied by two carts filled with wounded rebels.

quote.citation: 1918, W[illiam] B[abington] Maxwell, chapter V, in The Mirror and the Lamp, Indianapolis, Ind.: The Bobbs-Merrill Company, →OCLC:
quote.text: He was thinking; but the glory of the song, the swell from the great organ, the clustered lights,  […] , the height and vastness of this noble fane, its antiquity and its strength—all these things seemed to have their part as causes of the thrilling emotion that accompanied his thoughts.

definitions.definition: (intransitive, music) To perform an accompanying part or parts in a composition.
(transitive, music) To perform an accompanying part next to (another instrument or musician).
(intransitive, obsolete) To associate in a company; to keep company.

quote.citation: 1601, C[aius] Plinius Secundus [i.e., Pliny the Elder], “(please specify |book=I to XXXVII)”, in Philemon Holland, transl., The Historie of the World. Commonly Called, The Naturall Historie of C. Plinius Secundus. […], (please specify |tome=1 or 2), London:  […]  Adam Islip, →OCLC:
quote.text: Men say that they will drive away one another,  […]  and not accompanied together.

definitions.definition: (intransitive, obsolete) To cohabit (with). (Can we add an example for this sense?)
(transitive, obsolete) To cohabit with; to coexist with; occur with.

quote.citation: 1534, John Bourchier, 2nd Baron Berners, Golden Book of Marcus Aurelius:
quote.text: Gijb, Suche as accompanyeth with man-killers and murtherers.

definitions.definition: To be found at the same time.
